title: Punjab National Bank - 532461 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: PNB Q1 FY27 net profit INR5,253 crore; gross NPA fell to 2.78% from 3.78% year on year, and NIM rose to 2.64% domestic.
summary.overview: Punjab National Bank reported Q1 FY27 with gross advances up 12.7% YoY to INR12.73 lakh crore and global deposits up 8.5% to INR17.25 lakh crore. Management said it is shedding low-yielding advances (below 7% yield, roughly INR34,000-40,000 crore in the quarter) and IBPC exposure (INR22,411 crore YoY reduction), while core advances grew 15.4% excluding IBPC. Asset quality improved sharply, with gross NPA at 2.78% and net NPA at 0.28%, and the bank added INR390 crore of floating provision ahead of ECL implementation from 1 April 2027. Profit was flat quarter on quarter, which management attributed to this ECL-related provisioning.

segments.name: Retail (ex-IBPC)
segments.commentary: Retail book excluding IBPC grew 17.5% YoY; IBPC exposure is being run down from the retail portfolio. Personal loans total INR23,727 crore, all salaried-backed.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME book grew 19.8% YoY; management guides about 25% growth for the year, with digital cash-flow-based lending driving off-take. Management reports no stress in the book.

segments.name: Agriculture (priority sector)
segments.commentary: Agri priority sector grew 16.4% YoY. Gold loan book rose to about INR31,888 crore from INR15,694 crore a year earlier (about 103%), with a target of INR59,000-60,000 crore by year-end.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate loan book grew about 10%, with roughly INR35,000-40,000 crore of low-yielding corporate advances shed in Q1. Infrastructure is 9% of corporate book, energy 4%, roads and ports 4%, metals 1.8%, iron and steel about 2%.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Treasury income was about INR1,100 crore in Q1; management guides INR900-1,000 crore per quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects quarter-on-quarter improvement in NIM and NII in every coming quarter as higher-cost deposits reprice and low-yielding assets run off; FY27 NIM guidance reaffirmed.
Gross NPA guidance below 2.5% and net NPA below 0.3% for FY27; slippage ratio guidance below 0.9% (0.68% in Q1); PCR guidance above 96%.
Cost-to-income target of 47-48% by end FY27.

ECL transition: one-time impact estimated at INR9,500-10,000 crore, to be partly offset by floating provisions; recurring impact of 10-12 bp per quarter on credit cost. Final calculations due around October.
Plans to open 250 new branches in FY27, focused on southern and western regions. FY27 IT budget about INR3,400 crore.
FCNR(B) mobilisation target USD2.5 billion; USD425 million raised to date, of which about USD200 million came with a leverage product.
Expects to stop buying PSLC from next year, targeting sales of INR5,000-10,000 crore. PSLC cost fell to INR360 crore from INR893 crore a year ago.
Digital credit: target of another INR1 lakh crore of digital loan sanctions in FY27; Q1 digital sanctions above INR19,000 crore.
Bulk term deposits about 18% of deposits; deposit growth held at 8.5% to limit high-cost deposits.
capex_capacity: 250 new branches planned in FY27, with a focus on southern and western regions.
Gold loan banking extended to about 3,400 additional branches this year, on top of about 3,000 earlier.
New data centre in Gurgaon commissioned; FY27 IT and digital budget about INR3,400 crore against about 82-84% utilisation of the INR3,500 crore budget last year.
PNB has 10,300 branches, most in agri-dominated areas.
demand_pricing: Bank sanctioned over INR95,500 crore of credit in Q1 FY27, with INR1.38 lakh crore pending disbursement.
Cost of deposits fell 34 bp YoY; bank is not chasing bulk deposits or certificates of deposit.
Processing fees were INR938 crore vs INR728 crore a year earlier (about 29% growth), linked to corporate sanctions and turnaround-time improvements.
About INR15,000-17,000 crore of low-yielding corporate loans were allowed to exit rather than repriced; many others were repriced.
ECLGS: eligible amount INR40,000 crore; applications INR20,370 crore; sanctioned INR15,856 crore; disbursed INR12,335 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins versus private banks, and what is the FCNR target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher-cost deposit repricing was completed by May, deposit cost fell 34 bp YoY, and NIM should keep improving each quarter as low-yielding assets run off. FCNR target is USD2.5 billion, with USD425 million raised to date.

qa_highlights.question: SMA breakdown and ECL one-time impact?
qa_highlights.answer: SMA 0 is 1.55%, SMA 1 is 0.62% and SMA 2 is 0.73%, totalling 2.9%. The one-time ECL impact is about INR9,500-10,000 crore, with 10-12 bp per quarter recurring, and the floating provision will be used against migration.

qa_highlights.question: Why is QoQ profit flat, and why keep building floating provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is front-loading provisions (INR390 crore floating provision this quarter, INR2,435 crore cumulative) to avoid surprises when ECL starts on 1 April 2027. It said provisioning will run till 31 March.

qa_highlights.question: Opex and PSLC costs?
qa_highlights.answer: PSLC spend was INR360 crore in Q1 vs INR893 crore a year earlier, and management expects no PSLC purchases next year. Cost-to-income is expected to reach 47-48% by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Treasury outlook and IL&FS Tamil Nadu Power provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury income is guided at INR900-1,000 crore per quarter, with INR1,100 crore earned this quarter. About INR1,000 crore of provision is held on IL&FS Tamil Nadu Power and will be used in Q2 or Q3 with approvals in place.

qa_highlights.question: Stress in specific sectors and MSME outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reports no stress so far and says the SMA book is among its lowest in years. MSME growth is guided at about 25%, and most MSME loans are covered under CGTMSE at about 75%.

risks_watch: Flat quarterly profit (about INR5,200-5,253 crore) despite NII growth, because of ongoing floating provisions and ECL preparation.
ECL transition from 1 April 2027: one-time impact INR9,500-10,000 crore against the INR2,435 crore floating provision cushion, plus 10-12 bp of recurring credit cost per quarter.
Monsoon and El Niño risk to agri and MSME credit quality; management said it will assess August-September rainfall.
Gold loan book growth to INR59,000-60,000 crore by year-end, and the leverage uptake on FCNR(B) deposits.
Management's stated 'no material impact' from geopolitical tensions on asset quality; watch slippages against the 0.9% guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, asset quality and the bank's provisioning discipline; management repeated guidance and expects steady improvement. It was less specific on the reasons for flat QoQ profit and gave only qualitative answers on sector stress.
key_quotes: And this strategy is going to continue till we are coming out of all these low -yielding advances and you will see the improvement in the NII and the NIM in every quarter now onwards.
I think it is a very, very prudent decision of the management.
So in a true way all these floating provision which is there, I think that will be used for the migration purpose now.

growth.why: Management guides MSME growth around 25%, gold loans target INR59,000-60,000 crore by year-end, and 250 new branches in FY27, with a cost-to-income goal of 47-48%; backing is partly specific (branch rollout, 3,400 gold-loan branches, Rs1 lakh crore digital sanctions target) but the NIM and growth paths rely largely on repricing and demand.
